title: My work: what I own or decide
subtitle: Mock-ups for the owner to pick from: where My work lives, what it groups, and how it handles nothing, forty items and a viewer. Invented company, people and features.

decisions.name: Where My work lives
decisions.question: Where does a person find their own work, in Simple and in Detailed?
decisions.common: The same list of features and milestones I own, decisions I make and proposals I made, late and at risk first. Every feature row opens the one feature panel. The yellow count is late or at risk only, like the rail's other counts. A decision row carries its code, as on Decisions (Q5 Reminder default time).

proposals.name: Its own page
proposals.what: A My work entry under Home in the Simple rail, with a yellow count of late or at-risk items, and the same entry under Home in Detailed's rail. On a phone it takes One-pagers' place in the tab bar (One-pagers moves to More).
proposals.why: One place holds everything I own or decide, whatever the kind, and the rail count tells me when something slips without opening it. Home stays as it is.
proposals.plus: Same entry and page in Simple and Detailed; the page has room for forty items.
proposals.cost: 1 click from anywhere to see all my work; 2 to open a feature's panel. Today: no way to see it, only by opening each feature's panel on the Roadmap.

proposals.name: A Home section
proposals.what: A Yours card at the top of Home, Simple and Detailed: the first four items, then Show N more. Decisions stay in Home's existing decisions card, so Yours lists features, milestones and proposals only.
proposals.plus: No new page or rail entry; people already start on Home.
proposals.cost: 0 clicks to see the top four on Home, 1 more for the rest, 1 to open a panel. Home grows by one card, and pushes goals down.

Phone 390: Yours comes before the goals, so the goals start further down.

proposals.name: Mine on the Roadmap
proposals.what: A Mine button beside Key dates on the Roadmap shows only the features and milestones I own, by due date. Decisions stay on Decisions and proposals in the Inbox. No new entry in Detailed.
proposals.plus: No new page; it reuses the Roadmap that people already use to plan.
proposals.cost: 2 clicks to see my features (Roadmap, Mine); decisions take another page; 3 to open a panel. Today: no Mine at all.

decisions.name: What it groups
decisions.question: How does My work group my items, and what can I do on a row in one step?
decisions.common: Same items and the same one-step actions: a decision row (with its code) offers Decide as recommended or Another answer (as Home does today); a feature opens its panel; a proposal shows its replies; a milestone opens on the Roadmap. My work lists the 3 decisions with a due date and counts and links the 31 others on Decisions, so both say 34. A decided row stays with Undo, loses its Late tag, and every count drops at once: its group, the page, My work's and Decisions' rail counts. A commenter proposes instead of deciding; a viewer only opens.

proposals.name: By due date
proposals.what: One list in groups by when: Late or at risk, This week, Next week, Later, No date. Each row says what it is (Feature you own, You decide, Your proposal, Milestone you own).
proposals.why: It answers the question a person opens it with, what needs me first, and puts overdue and at-risk items on top whatever their kind, as the issue asks.
proposals.plus: One scan from top to bottom; nothing late hides in a lower group.
proposals.cost: Decide as recommended: 1 click on the row. Another answer: 3 clicks (Another answer, pick, Decide). Today: Decisions page, find it, then the same 1 to 3 clicks.

proposals.name: By what I do
proposals.what: Four lists by kind: Waiting for your decision, Features you own, Milestones coming up, Proposals you made; late and at risk first inside each.
proposals.plus: Clear which hat I am wearing; easy to skip a whole kind.
proposals.cost: Same clicks per row as a; a late feature can sit below three on-time decisions.

Hard case, forty items at 1512: the late features start below all the decisions.

proposals.name: Counts first
proposals.what: Four count tiles, like Home's summary: decisions to make, features you own, milestones coming up, proposals you made. Picking a tile lists that kind under it.
proposals.plus: The whole picture in one line; the page stays short with forty items.
proposals.cost: 1 extra click on a tile before any row; 4 clicks to decide another answer. Late items of other kinds stay hidden until their tile is picked.

Hard case, forty items at 1512: tiles stay one line; features you own lists five, then Show 21 more.
Phone 390: four tiles two by two, the picked list under them.

decisions.name: Nothing, forty, a viewer
decisions.question: What does My work show when I own nothing, when I own forty items, and to a viewer?
decisions.common: The same page and grouping (MW1 a, MW2 a). One short line and an (i) when nothing is mine. A viewer who owns nothing sees that line and its (i), with no button or link, in every proposal; it is drawn once, in a.

proposals.name: Take from No owner
proposals.what: Empty: Pick features to own opens the features with no owner yet, each with Take it; Done puts them in My work. Forty: five per group, then Show N more. Viewer: the line and its (i) only.
proposals.why: Most features read No owner yet today; this turns the empty page into the one-click way to own one, which the issue asks for, and keeps long lists short without a new control.
proposals.plus: Owning a feature drops from 5 steps to 1 click each.
proposals.cost: Own two features: 4 clicks (Pick, Take it, Take it, Done). Today: 5 steps each on the Roadmap, 10 for two.

A viewer who owns nothing: the line and its (i), no button.
Phone 390 with forty items: five per group keeps the page short.

proposals.name: Oracle suggests
proposals.what: Empty: Suggest what I could own asks Oracle for three features with a reason each (you wrote its one-pager, you run its track); Confirm or Not this, as for Oracle's other suggestions. Forty: one line per item and a Find box.
proposals.plus: Suggestions come with a reason; forty items fit on two screens.
proposals.cost: Own two: 4 clicks (Suggest, Confirm, Confirm, Done); only Oracle's three show. Forty: typing to find.

Phone 390 with forty items: one-line rows wrap long names.

proposals.name: Point to the Roadmap
proposals.what: Empty: one line with a link, Set owners on the Roadmap; owners are set in each feature's panel as today. Forty: ten a page with Back and Next 10.
proposals.plus: Nothing new to build for owning; one way to set an owner.
proposals.cost: Own one feature: 5 steps (link, find it on the Roadmap, open it, Owner Change, pick); 10 for two. Forty: 4 pages.
